children: Visa, the global payments and transaction-security company

, open-sourced part of its AI-driven vulnerability-defense system, with shares down approximately 0.7% to $363.19 at 11.04am ET on September 30. According to Reuters, the move comes as the industry braces for cyberattacks that can adapt. The goal is simple: find weak spots and fix them before attackers get there.

Visa's Vulnerability Agentic Harness maps software, identifies and ranks weaknesses, recommends fixes and checks whether those changes work. Human review remains a checkpoint before findings or patches move forward. Visa says an early update developed with Anthropic's assistance found more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in its first month. That is a sizeable detection tally. The real test is how quickly teams can turn those findings into verified fixes.

Opening the framework could draw outside testing and distribute development work, while giving rivals access to the same tools. Visa's lasting edge will depend on its network data and execution. The valuation graphic puts shares 10.37% below the $405.23 GF Value estimate, suggesting a discount without proving the stock is cheap. For a payments network, stronger security protects the asset that matters most: trust.

title: Visa Stocks Fall as Open Cyber Defense Answers Agentic Threats
